name: graph_algorithms
title: Graph Algorithms
summary: Provides tools to analyze graphs given as edge lists, computing shortest paths, connectivity, minimum spanning trees, maximum flow, centrality, and triangle counts.

tools.name: shortest_path_weight
tools.description: Computes the shortest weighted path length between two nodes in a graph.

params.name: edges
params.description: A list of edges, where each edge is represented as [node1, node2, weight]. If weight is omitted, it defaults to 1.

params.name: source
params.description: The starting node for the path.

params.name: target
params.description: The ending node for the path.

returns.name: weight
returns.description: The shortest path length (sum of weights).

returns.name: path_exists
returns.description: Whether a path exists between the source and target.

returns.name: display
returns.description: A human-readable summary of the result (e.g., 'Shortest path weight from A to C is 15' or 'No path exists').

tools.implementation_notes: Import networkx as nx. Create a nx.Graph(). Add edges using G.add_weighted_edges_from(edges). Call nx.dijkstra_path_length(G, source, target, weight='weight'). Handle nx.NetworkXNoPath by returning path_exists=False and weight=None. Construct the display string based on the result.

tools.name: count_connected_components
tools.description: Returns the number of connected components in an undirected graph.

params.name: edges
params.description: A list of edges, where each edge is [node1, node2].

returns.name: display
returns.description: A human-readable summary (e.g., 'The graph has 2 connected components').

returns.name: is_connected
returns.description: True if the graph is connected (count == 1), False otherwise.

tools.implementation_notes: Import networkx as nx. Create a nx.Graph(). Add edges using G.add_edges_from(edges). Call nx.number_connected_components(G). Set is_connected = (count == 1).

tools.name: mst_total_weight
tools.description: Computes the total weight of the minimum spanning tree (or forest) of an undirected graph.

params.name: edges
params.description: A list of edges, where each edge is [node1, node2, weight].

returns.name: total_weight
returns.description: The sum of the weights of the edges in the minimum spanning tree.

returns.name: mst_edges
returns.description: The edges included in the MST, formatted as [node1, node2, weight].

returns.name: display
returns.description: A human-readable summary (e.g., 'The total weight of the MST is 3').

tools.implementation_notes: Import networkx as nx. Create a nx.Graph(). Add edges using G.add_weighted_edges_from(edges). Call T = nx.minimum_spanning_tree(G, weight='weight'). Calculate total_weight as sum(d['weight'] for u, v, d in T.edges(data=True)). Return T.edges(data='weight') as a list of [u, v, w].

tools.name: max_flow_value
tools.description: Computes the maximum flow value between a source and a sink node in a capacitated graph.

params.name: edges
params.description: A list of edges, where each edge is [node1, node2, capacity].

returns.name: flow_value
returns.description: The value of the maximum flow.

returns.name: display
returns.description: A human-readable summary (e.g., 'The maximum flow from S to T is 5').

tools.implementation_notes: Import networkx as nx. Create a nx.DiGraph(). For each edge [u, v, c] in edges, call G.add_edge(u, v, capacity=c). Call nx.maximum_flow_value(G, source, target, capacity='capacity').

tools.name: highest_betweenness_centrality_node
tools.description: Identifies the node with the highest betweenness centrality in a graph.

params.name: edges
params.description: A list of edges, where each edge is [node1, node2].

params.name: weight_attribute
params.description: The attribute name for edge weights. If omitted, weights are assumed to be 1.

returns.name: node
returns.description: The node with the highest betweenness centrality.

returns.name: centrality_value
returns.description: The betweenness centrality value of that node.

returns.name: display
returns.description: A human-readable summary (e.g., 'Node B has the highest betweenness centrality of 0.6').

tools.implementation_notes: Import networkx as nx. Create a nx.Graph(). Add edges. If weight_attribute is provided, use G.add_weighted_edges_from(edges). Call centralities = nx.betweenness_centrality(G, weight=weight_attribute). Find the node with the max value in the centralities dictionary.

tools.name: count_triangles
tools.description: Computes the total number of unique triangles in an undirected graph.

params.name: edges
params.description: A list of edges, where each edge is [node1, node2].

returns.name: total_triangles
returns.description: The total number of unique triangles in the graph.

returns.name: display
returns.description: A human-readable summary (e.g., 'The graph contains 1 unique triangle').

tools.implementation_notes: Import networkx as nx. Create a nx.Graph(). Add edges using G.add_edges_from(edges). Call tri_dict = nx.triangles(G). Calculate total_triangles = sum(tri_dict.values()) // 3.

uncertainties: The tools assume the input edges are for an undirected graph unless specified (e.g., max_flow_value uses DiGraph).
The behavior for empty graphs or graphs with only one node is dependent on the library's implementation.
